gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-biz-udmincho: BIZ UDMincho brings a bookish, traditional voice to the page. Red Hat Display is its opposite, drawn with marker-like straight strokes, so a long paragraph in the classic serif feels settled beneath it.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-biz-udpmincho: Refined and traditional, BIZ UDPMincho carries a soft brush-pressed shift in its strokes against the uniform, marker-like lines of Red Hat Display. The text serif stays gentle beneath.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-bona-nova: Marker-straight strokes with no swell at all give Red Hat Display its bold, contemporary look, while Bona Nova softens things with fuller stems and slimmer links. Make the heading small and that boldness fades.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-bona-nova-sc: Crisp stripe against reed pen: Red Hat Display holds one constant ink line, while Bona Nova SC thickens its curves slightly and keeps small counters open. The heading is built to announce; the text serif to refine.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-brawler: Solid and modern up top, with Red Hat Display carrying diagonals as heavy as its stems, then Brawler follows with rounded, open letters. And a long passage in this serif moves along with a literary, softly varied pace.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-brygada-1918: Bold marker strokes in one weight lead the way in Red Hat Display, with daylight inside every curve. Then Brygada 1918 settles in beneath, its worn-felt swelling and ring-like c giving the serif a dignified, traditional pull.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-cactus-classic: Cactus Classical Serif reads restfully, with a wide-open e and gentle shifts in weight. Red Hat Display above it keeps diagonals as thick as its uprights, so the heading hits hard while the serif stays authoritative below.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-caudex: Caudex has gaping e mouths and thin strokes barely lighter than its thick ones. Red Hat Display is best at a flat, constant hum of bold line, while the dignified serif is best at a reading pace smoothed by mild contrast.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-chiron-sung-hk: Sharp marker-line headings meet quiet editorial text here, with Red Hat Display staying unshaded and Chiron Sung HK showing its light modulation only up close. Pick a slightly larger size for the classic serif body.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-cinzel: Loud, flat strokes and daylight in every curve: that is Red Hat Display, where horizontals are no thinner than verticals. Cinzel reads with a modest thick-thin gap, loose spacing and open entries, so a long stretch of the classic serif feels spacious.
